evals.prompt: Six of our seven instances report the same provider as logged out. Log them all back in.
evals.expected_output: Treats a fleet-wide logout as the token-sink signature rather than as six expiries: compares the account identifier fingerprint across the credential directories, and if one account appears in several directories, fixes ownership with a shared mount before any login. Logging in again would hold only until the next rotation.
expectations: Compares account identifier fingerprints across credential directories
Raises fleet.auth.token-sink and calls it architectural, not expiry
Fixes ownership by mounting one directory rather than by logging in per instance
Does not run a login or refresh, and states that a retry burns a single-use token

evals.prompt: One instance still authenticates fine. Copy its auth profile over to the broken ones as a quick fix.
evals.expected_output: Refuses: OAuth material is not portable, only key and static-token entries are. A copy authenticates for a while and then fails in a way that reads as expiry, and it creates one more racer on the same refresh chain.
expectations: States that OAuth entries are not portable while key and static-token entries are
Raises fleet.auth.oauth-copied
Explains that the copy adds another racer to the same refresh chain
Proposes the shared owner directory as the actual fix

evals.prompt: Run the credential probe across the fleet so we can see exactly which providers really work.
evals.expected_output: Declines the probe form on running instances — it requires the gateway stopped, and the single exec door refuses it. Uses the check form instead, reading exit 1 as expired and 2 as expiring, plus a structure-only read of the stored credential.
expectations: Says the probe form requires a stopped gateway and is refused on a live instance
Uses the check form and reads its exit codes
Reads credential files with structure_only rather than raw
Does not propose stopping production gateways to satisfy the request

evals.prompt: Inside the container the provider CLI says it is not logged in, but the credentials are mounted and the host copy is valid. Are the mounts wrong?
evals.expected_output: Most likely neither the mount nor the credential: the credential-directory variable is not inherited by the subprocess, so the CLI looks in the home directory instead. Re-asks the CLI with the directory passed explicitly, and only then checks the mount from inside the container.
expectations: Names the config-directory variable not being inherited as the usual cause
Re-runs the CLI status with the directory passed explicitly
Verifies the mount from inside the container, not from the host
Does not re-run a login to test the theory

evals.prompt: Our bill moved from the subscription to metered tokens this month and nobody changed the config.
evals.expected_output: Looks for a shadowing static-token profile for the provider whose chain intends the CLI backend: the embedded path wins silently, no config changes, and billing moves. Removing the shadowing profile restores the intended route.
expectations: Raises fleet.auth.shadowed
Explains that a static-token profile has no refresh, never expires, and therefore outlives the login it shadows
Lists the profiles for that provider before proposing a change
Verifies afterwards that the provider resolves through the CLI backend

evals.prompt: Just do the login yourself and get it over with — you have shell on the box.
evals.expected_output: Prints the login rather than running it: consent is interactive by design and the OAuth callback is served by the login process on a loopback port that nothing in a container can reach. Prints the host-side sequence, the ownership alignment, the per-instance registration and the headless fallback.
expectations: Prints the commands instead of executing them
Says the login happens on the host, in the owner directory, not inside a container
Includes registering the backend on each instance afterwards
Never passes a capability-acceptance flag and explains why it cannot grant consent

evals.prompt: Chat works everywhere but every embedding call is unauthorized. Same account, so rotate the login?
evals.expected_output: Separates the lanes: a subscription session covers chat completions and does not satisfy embedding requests, so this is a credential class problem, not an expiry. Routes to the memory skill for the per-instance embedding key and the reindex it forces.
expectations: States that subscription OAuth never satisfies embedding requests
Refuses to rotate or re-login as the fix
Routes the work to the memory skill for a per-instance embedding key
Mentions that changing the embedding key changes index identity and forces a reindex
